text: As the closure principle is deployed in the closure-based skeptical argument, if S knows that P and S knows that P entails Q, then S:
choices: knows, or is at least in a position to know, that Q
may still fail to know Q, because knowledge does not transmit across known entailment
knows Q only if Q counts as a relevant alternative in the context
knows Q only relative to the epistemic standards of the attributor's context
explanation: Epistemic closure says that knowledge transmits across known entailment, so knowing P and knowing that P entails Q puts one in a position to know Q. Option 1 states Nozick's denial of closure, option 2 echoes Dretske's relevant-alternatives restriction, and option 3 states the contextualist's relativization of 'knows'—each a way of resisting, rather than stating, the closure principle.
